about: The team's conversation workflow for chicken chop with pasta, as a script. scripts/run_workflow.py plays each user line through the backend and prints the reply next to the ideal one. Section 1 is the opening conversation (the recipe is already chosen in the app).

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.instruction: Halve the six cherry tomatoes and finely chop one small garlic clove.
steps.check: The tomatoes are halved and the garlic is finely chopped.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.instruction: Open the chicken thigh out flat on a separate plate, then season both sides with a little salt and pepper.
steps.check: The chicken is flat and seasoned on both sides.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.instruction: Add one teaspoon of oil to the frying pan, then put it over medium heat.
steps.check: The oil moves easily across the pan and looks slightly shimmery.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.instruction: Using tongs, gently lower the chicken into the pan. Let the underside brown before turning it, then cook the other side.

steps.title: Check the chicken
steps.instruction: Cut into the thickest part. The centre should no longer be pink and the juices should run clear. If you have a thermometer, it should read 75°C.
steps.check: The centre is no longer pink.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.instruction: Fill a saucepan with enough water for the pasta to move freely and bring it to a boil. Add the pasta, stir, and cook it for the time on the packet.
steps.check: The pasta is tender but not mushy.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.instruction: In a small saucepan, warm the remaining teaspoon of oil with the garlic over low heat until fragrant, without letting it brown. Add the cherry tomatoes and 100 grams of tomato sauce, stir, and simmer gently.
steps.check: The tomatoes have softened into a smooth sauce.

steps.title: Bring it together
steps.instruction: Turn off the pasta, save a little pasta water, then drain it. Add the pasta to the sauce and toss gently until coated. Serve with the chicken and a little grated cheese if you like.
steps.check: The pasta is coated in sauce and plated next to the chicken.

turns.ideal: Lovely. Have you got the tomato sauce, cherry tomatoes and garlic as well?

turns.user: I've got the sauce and cherry tomatoes, and some cheese.
Yes, I have garlic too. Let's start.
How fine does the garlic need to be?
turns.ideal: Small pieces are fine, it's up to you.

turns.user: Those are ready. What about the chicken?
How will I know when to add the chicken?
turns.ideal: When the oil moves easily across the pan and looks slightly shimmery. If it starts smoking, turn the heat down.

turns.user: Should I keep moving it around?
turns.ideal: Leave it in place for now. Once it browns, it should lift more easily.

turns.user: Can you have a look? I'm worried I'm burning it.
turns.ideal: The surface looks golden brown, with a darker patch near the edge. Turn the heat down a little if it's browning too quickly.

turns.user: I've cut into the thickest part. Can you see the middle?
turns.ideal: I can see the cut surface, but the middle is partly in shadow. Could you move the plate into better light?
Yes, that's clearer. The visible centre looks opaque, though a photo can't confirm that chicken is cooked through.

turns.user: So you can check how it looks, but you can't tell me for sure?
turns.ideal: That's right. Use my camera check as a reference only, not as proof.

turns.user: The water's boiling and the pasta's in. The packet says ten minutes.
turns.ideal: Would you like a ten-minute timer?

turns.user: The sauce looks a bit thick.
turns.ideal: Stir in a tablespoon of the pasta water. You can add another if it still looks too thick.

turns.user: The pasta is still a little too firm for me.
turns.ideal: Give it another minute. Would you like a one-minute timer?
I can see the chicken beside the pasta, and the pasta looks coated in the sauce. You can add a little grated cheese if you'd like.

turns.user: Sure, I'm a cheese fan for real.
